svg.title: Figure 3-SG-01-1. SG-01: from the fault tree to the FMEA
svg.desc: Figure 3-SG-01-1. SG-01: 28 events (backed 26, by design 1, external 1, unbacked 0); 74 FMEA modes reach SG-01 (in the tree 60, justified 14, tree gaps 0). Single points: BE-1.01: SWF-001, SFM-002, 8 causes, D 3–10, partly detected; BE-1.10: DFM-019, 2 causes, D 10, not detected; BE-1.18: PFM-001, 1 causes, D 5, partly detected. BE-1.01 (Envelope torque limits set above the controllable bound (raw 1500/15/25/450 not derived, GAP-04; identical in controller, CCF → DFI-08)) → SWF-001, SFM-002: Steering request above the torque or torque-rate limit for the vehicle is passed; worst cause SFM-002.C1 (Lateral controller output too high (gain, torque model, saturation logic); O 7, D 10, AP H); detection: test_latcontrol.py covers saturation only; test_latcontrol_torque_buffer.py covers the request buffer only; nothing checks controller state across disengagement BE-1.10 (Frame corrupted after safety_tx_hook in a part not covered by the packet XOR: copy into FDCAN message RAM, message RAM itself, FDCAN core, transceiver (the 8-bit XOR checked before loading, fdcan.h:100, covers only the software TX queue)) → DFM-019: Approved CAN frame altered between the TX check and the bus; worst cause DFM-019.C1 (Soft error or permanent fault in the copy into FDCAN message RAM, the message RAM or the FDCAN core. The packet XOR is checked at the FDCAN load (fdcan.h:100) and covers only the software queue; the CAN CRC is computed after the fault; O 3, D 10, AP H); detection: No LionDriver hardware verification or qualification test exists for this cause (WP-H-06/WP-H-07 not started; no HIL bench, D-04) BE-1.02 (controlsd/card software fault (QM)) → SFM-002, SFM-003, SWF-042, SWF-059, SWF-076, SWF-077, SWF-079: Steering torque or torque rate above limits; worst cause SFM-002.C1 (Lateral controller output too high (gain, torque model, saturation logic); O 7, D 10, AP H); detection: test_latcontrol.py covers saturation only; test_latcontrol_torque_buffer.py covers the request buffer only; nothing checks controller state across disengagement BE-1.03 (Wrong desired curvature from model) → SFM-002, SFM-003, PFM-009, PFM-012: Steering torque or torque rate above limits; worst cause SFM-002.C1 (Lateral controller output too high (gain, torque model, saturation logic); O 7, D 10, AP H); detection: test_latcontrol.py covers saturation only; test_latcontrol_torque_buffer.py covers the request buffer only; nothing checks controller state across disengagement BE-1.04 (Debug/maneuver process replaces controller (process_config.py:34-47, GAP-20)) → SWF-049: Desired curvature taken from the developer lateral-maneuver plan instead of the driving model; worst cause SWF-049.C1 (controlsd uses lateralManeuverPlan whenever its last message was valid (controlsd.py:123-124), with no alive check (SubMaster valid changes only on receipt, cereal/messaging/__init__.py:261) and no check of the mode; selfdrived ignores lateralManeuverPlan in its alive/valid checks (selfdrived.py:87). Up to BL-006 the path was enabled by the LateralManeuverMode developer toggle. Since DQ-131 A (be0b4ff, BL-007) the reference build neither registers nor ships lateral_maneuversd, maneuversd or joystick (process_config.py REFERENCE_EXCLUDED_PROCS), so nothing publishes lateralManeuverPlan, and selfdrived refuses engagement while a debug param is set (DQ-221 A). Remaining: the subscription and the path stay in controlsd, and the processes come back in a build that carries the upstream_build marker (a build-path defect, as SWF-013.C2); O 3, D 4, AP L); detection: Proven by mutation in CI (after BL-007): the tests fail on each hand-written mutant of this cause (PC-1, PC-2), tools/ci/host_mutation.py in the tests.yaml unit_tests job; so D 4 (RT-2), from D 8 BE-1.05 (Wrong CarParams / fingerprint (CCF → DFI-09)) → SFM-032, PFM-013, SWF-058: Wrong vehicle configuration active (fingerprint or car port); worst cause SWF-058.C2 (The FINGERPRINT environment variable overrides identification, and cached CarParams FW are reused when the VIN is known, so a replaced ECU is not re-queried (car_helpers.py:93-98, 140-142); O 2, D 10, AP H); detection: No test targets this cause BE-1.24 (Command corrupted on the SoC-to-MCU SPI link and accepted: both checks are 8-bit XOR over the same bytes, no counter (spi.cc:189-202, panda.cc:284-290) (random HW)) → DFM-015, SWF-026: Corrupted SoC-to-MCU transfer accepted; worst cause DFM-015.C1 (Bit errors on the SPI link (EMC, signal integrity); 8-bit XOR only, no sequence counter; O 4, D 10, AP H); detection: No LionDriver hardware verification or qualification test exists for this cause (WP-H-06/WP-H-07 not started; no HIL bench, D-04) BE-1.06 (Envelope software defect in lateral checks (lateral.h:60-151)) → SWF-001, SWF-016: Steering request above the torque or torque-rate limit for the vehicle is passed; worst cause SWF-001.C1 (Panda torque limits (max 1500, rate up 15 / down 25, error 350) are the same constants as the SoC controller's and are not derived from a vehicle envelope; O 6, D 9, AP H); detection: No test targets this cause BE-1.07 (MCU execution fault (RAM/register/CPU) corrupts limit or check, not detected (no MPU, no ECC handling, faults report-only; GAP-08)) → DFM-001, DFM-002, DFM-003, DFM-005, DFM-007, DFM-018: Safety check computes a wrong result (permanent CPU or data-path fault); worst cause DFM-007.C1 (Vehicle supply dip (cranking, alternator fault) with BOR level not set and PVD not enabled; O 5, D 10, AP H); detection: No LionDriver hardware verification or qualification test exists for this cause (WP-H-06/WP-H-07 not started; no HIL bench, D-04) BE-1.08 (Safety mode/param changed by SoC (0xdc, GAP-09) [FFI → FFI-CM-06; CCF → DFI-13: same SoC fault can cause G-SoC and BE-1.08]) → SWF-013, SWF-022: Wrong or permissive safety mode accepted from the host; worst cause SWF-022.C1 (setSafetyMode writes safety_configs[0] model and param and alternative_experience exactly as found in CarParams (panda_safety.cc:56-70). There is no allow-list for the reference configuration. A fingerprinting or CarParams error, such as a wrong EPS factor or flags, reaches the panda. At BL-004 the panda accepted any mode; at BL-005 the reference lock refuses anything but TOYOTA/73 (SWF-013), so the remaining effect is the safe direction (no engagement); O 7, D 10, AP H); detection: No test targets this cause; test_pandad.py (hardware) checks only that pandad starts BE-1.09 (Envelope firmware replaced via boot pins / softloader (GAP-38, GAP-24) [FFI → FFI-CM-12; CCF → DFI-13]) → SWF-028, PFM-001, DFM-016, PFM-002, SWF-084: pandad runs against panda firmware that is not the assured reference build; worst cause SWF-028.C1 (pandad.py and up_to_date() compare the panda signature with the panda_h7.bin.signed built from the checkout (pandad.py:16-18, 29-49; panda.cc:116-127). At BL-004 that build was not LIONDRIVER_REFERENCE. At BL-005 it is by default, and pandad checks the reference-build flag (TSR-619). Remaining: the flag says "a reference build", not "the assured release image" (any LIONDRIVER_REFERENCE build of any commit sets it), and a build opted out on both sides passes; O 5, D 10, AP H); detection: No host test of the pandad check. The panda side (flag set only in the reference build) is unit-tested in panda CI; the release build check is in CI (SWF-013.C2). Neither is designed to detect a non-assured reference image UE-1.11 (EPS does not limit LKA torque to an overpowerable level (AOU-01R fails)): No FMEA row needed: external; AOU-01R BE-1.12 (Corrupted/replayed 0x1D2 creates false cruise rising edge with valid 8-bit checksum (no counter, GAP-01)) → SWF-007: Controls allowed without a driver engagement; worst cause SWF-007.C1 (Defect in pcm_cruise_check or PCM_CRUISE decoding (toyota.h rx hook, 0x1D2 bit 5); O 5, D 3, AP H); detection: opendbc safety suite with 100% line coverage and mutation tests, run by fork CI on every change (.github/workflows/safety.yaml, CR-CI-05). At BL-002 the Toyota tests pass locally (287, 34 skipped); mutation was last run locally at BL-001 (2705/2705 killed). Tests are derived from the implementation, not from requirements BE-1.13 (Panda RX path delivers stale/stuck cruise frame to both envelope and SoC (single RX path; CCF → DFI-10)) → SWF-006: Stale brake, cruise or EPS data used beyond the detection budget; worst cause SWF-006.C1 (An RX check lags only after 5 nominal periods plus one 10 ms safety-task period (0x1D2 about 0.16 s, 0x226 about 0.14 s, 0x260 0.11 s, 0xAA about 0.07 s); the budget is not yet confirmed against an FTTI (HARA OI-004) or against real inter-frame gaps (tools/can_gaps); O 4, D 3, AP H); detection: Per-message 5-period timeout test for every Toyota RX check, in the CI safety suite BE-1.14 (MCU fault sets controls_allowed (BE-1.07 class)) → DFM-003: Safety state in SRAM corrupted (controls_allowed, limits, counters, stack); worst cause DFM-003.C1 (Double-bit soft error or permanent SRAM fault; RAMECC monitors not configured, ECC interrupt not registered; O 3, D 10, AP H); detection: No LionDriver hardware verification or qualification test exists for this cause (WP-H-06/WP-H-07 not started; no HIL bench, D-04) BE-1.25 (Envelope software defect in the not-allowed torque check or the controls_allowed bookkeeping (lateral.h:111-114), e.g. a cruise edge refused for MAIN_ON = 0 left the engagement window open (SM-F1, SWF-089; reference build fixed at BL-006, opendbc#17)) → SWF-002, SWF-055, SWF-089: Steering torque passed while controls are not allowed; worst cause SWF-002.C1 (Defect in the not-allowed torque check (lateral.h:111-114) or in controls_allowed bookkeeping; O 5, D 3, AP H); detection: opendbc safety suite with 100% line coverage and mutation tests, run by fork CI on every change (.github/workflows/safety.yaml, CR-CI-05). At BL-002 the Toyota tests pass locally (287, 34 skipped); mutation was last run locally at BL-001 (2705/2705 killed). Tests are derived from the implementation, not from requirements BE-1.15 (SoC commands non-zero torque (normally gated by its own engagement state, which is fed by the same CAN data — CCF → DFI-10)) → SFM-001, SWF-041, SFM-013, SWF-030, SWF-057: Steering torque applied when not engaged; worst cause SWF-057.C2 (Short frames are not rejected: the parser skips only frames over 64 bytes and reads missing bytes as 0 (parser.py:219, dbc.py:66), so a truncated BRAKE_MODULE reads BRAKE_PRESSED = 0 with no checksum to catch it. Host code unchanged at BL-006; the panda-side length fault is implemented in the reference build since BL-006 (opendbc#18, a safety mechanism of SWF-057); O 3, D 10, AP H); detection: No test targets this cause BE-1.16 (Brake 0x226 lost/stuck "not pressed" (no checksum, no counter, timeout ≈2 s; GAP-01, GAP-06). 2026-10-12: loss detected ≤ 0.162 s (5 periods, 100 Hz; WP-S-04 T-01); stuck undetected) → SWF-006, SWF-005: Stale brake, cruise or EPS data used beyond the detection budget; worst cause SWF-005.C1 (BRAKE_MODULE (0x226) has no checksum or counter in the vehicle DBC; the RX check ignores checksum, counter and quality and checks timing only; O 3, D 9, AP H); detection: No test targets this cause

svg.text: SG-01: 28 events (backed 26, by design 1, external 1, unbacked 0); 74 FMEA modes reach SG-01 (in the tree 60, justified 14, tree gaps 0)
Worst cause: highest AP, then highest D. Red: single-point path from the gate logic. Text cut with … is given in full in the figure description.
